title: Signal · Monday 16 November
overview: A quiet weekend: JPMorgan blocks AI shopping agents from its customers' cards, the FBI warns that the ARTEX AI attack framework is hitting financial firms, and BaFin fines Deutsche Bank over its Postbank migration.

top.headline: JPMorgan blocks AI shopping agents from using its customers' credit cards
top.summary: JPMorgan Chase is blocking AI agents from shopping with its customers' credit cards when customers give an agent their card number, The Wall Street Journal reported on 13 November, according to PYMNTS. Cards from Bank of America, Capital One and Citigroup are already used by agents when customers allow it. Stripe gets round the block with one-time virtual cards, which merchants say cost more to accept.
top.background: Outside agents already cannot log in with Chase credentials, send money or pay bills. On the bank's third-quarter call, chief executive Jamie Dimon warned against "rogue agents".
top.why: The largest US bank is setting the terms on which agents may spend customers' money, on the day ChatGPT Wallet launched. Swiss and European issuers face the same choice between blocking agents and offering bounded, tokenised access.
top.watch_next: Whether JPMorgan adopts Visa and Mastercard agentic tokens, which hide the card number and carry the shopper's limits; the Journal says it has been slow to.

top.headline: FBI warns the ARTEX AI attack framework is hitting financial firms and others
top.summary: In a FLASH advisory released on 13 November, the FBI said several threat actors have used ARTEX, an open-source framework whose AI agents handle reconnaissance, exploitation and data theft, since at least August against financial, government, technology, defence and healthcare organisations, according to BleepingComputer. Some intrusions reached privileged access in under three hours. The 13-page advisory lists indicators of compromise.
top.background: ARTEX has no model of its own and drives external ones, including Claude, GPT, DeepSeek, GLM, Grok and Kimi. Its author pulled it from GitHub on 8 October, but forks and a commercial ARTEX PRO remain.
top.why: The FBI puts official weight behind earlier research: attacks now chain steps in hours and favour partner portals, legacy services and third-party integrations, which tests banks' response times and supplier reviews.
top.watch_next: Whether European and Swiss cyber authorities issue their own ARTEX guidance for financial institutions.

top.headline: BaFin fines Deutsche Bank EUR 8 million over its Postbank IT migration
top.summary: Germany's financial supervisor BaFin fined Deutsche Bank EUR 8 million under the Securities Trading Act over Project Unity, which moved Postbank customers onto the parent bank's IT system, according to Fintech News Switzerland. BaFin found that in 2023 the bank lacked arrangements to handle the surge in complaints promptly and was slow to transfer securities accounts. EUR 5.5 million covers the complaints and EUR 2.5 million the late transfers.
top.background: The fines were imposed on 11 November. Under the Act, a request to move a securities account counts as a client order and must be completed within three weeks at most.
top.why: It turns a migration backlog into a priced conduct breach. Banks planning core moves, including Swiss banks changing platforms, will be asked how they would absorb a spike in complaints and transfers.

items.headline: Sygnum launches a market-neutral fund that pays its returns in ether
items.summary: Digital asset bank Sygnum launched its ETH Alpha Fund SP for qualified and professional investors, targeting 8 to 10 percent a year in ETH after fees, against about 2 to 3 percent from staking alone, the company said. Core holdings stay staked with Sygnum; options premiums, arbitrage and funding rates add the rest.
items.why: Swiss crypto banks are moving from custody and staking to managed yield products, a benchmark for private banks that offer digital assets to clients.

items.headline: UK platform bank Griffin raises USD 20 million for cards and stablecoins
items.summary: Griffin, a UK bank serving fintechs and platforms, raised USD 20 million in a Series B led by Octagon Partners, valuing it at more than USD 100 million. It says the money carries it to profitability and funds branded debit cards, then credit cards, plus reserve services for stablecoin firms. More than 80 firms, including Uber, use it.
items.why: Licensed infrastructure banks are adding stablecoin services beside cards, a model Swiss banks serving fintech and crypto clients will recognise.

items.headline: Visa partners can now settle in Western Union's USDPT stablecoin via Anchorage
items.summary: Anchorage Digital is working with Visa so that some stablecoins it issues can settle on the card network, starting with Western Union's USDPT, which Visa and eligible partners can now use to pay what they owe on VisaNet. The firms did not say which partners or markets qualify.
items.why: Card-network settlement in a bank-issued stablecoin moves tokenised money closer to everyday treasury work at banks and their payment providers.

items.headline: Glarus asks its cantonal bank to build capital and keep payouts steady
items.summary: The Glarus government adopted a new owner strategy for Glarner Kantonalbank on 10 November, replacing the 2008 version, finews reported. The canton keeps its majority stake and the state guarantee, and wants equity built from the bank's own earnings, backed by an expectation of "steady, non-maximised" distributions (translated from German).
items.why: A guarantor canton putting the bank's capital ahead of its own payouts reduces the risk it carries through the state guarantee.

items.headline: Swiss pension funds gain 0.41 percent in October as Swiss shares rise 6 percent
items.summary: Swiss pension funds returned 0.41 percent on average in October and 4.91 percent so far this year, according to UBS's pension fund performance study, reported by finews. Swiss equities gained 6.01 percent while global equities fell 2.84 percent, the weakest asset class. Funds with under CHF 300 million in assets did slightly better than those above CHF 1 billion.
items.why: A strong home market is carrying Swiss portfolios while global equities and alternatives lag, which shapes the allocation conversations pension clients bring to their banks.

items.headline: Update: Rohner ordered Credit Suisse's surveillance of Greenpeace, SonntagsZeitung reports
items.summary: Former Credit Suisse chair Urs Rohner personally ordered the surveillance of Greenpeace after activists abseiled from the ceiling at the bank's 2017 annual meeting, the SonntagsZeitung reported, according to cash.ch's weekend press review, which marks such reports as unverified. When the affair surfaced in 2020, former COO Pierre-Olivier Bouée was suspected of ordering it.
items.why: Days after the finance ministry fined Rohner over false information to FINMA, the report ties the former chair more directly to the operation itself.

items.headline: Generali lifts its nine-month operating result 8.5 percent despite heavier catastrophe losses
items.summary: Generali's operating result rose 8.5 percent to EUR 6,446 million in the first nine months, gross written premiums grew 4.5 percent to EUR 76.5 billion and life net inflows rose 13.6 percent to EUR 11.7 billion, the group said on 13 November. Property and casualty absorbed over EUR 1 billion more from natural catastrophes and large man-made events.
items.why: After Allianz and Zurich, it rounds off a strong quarter for Europe's large insurers, whose growing asset and wealth arms compete with private banks for savings.

items.headline: LangChain raises USD 300 million at a USD 3 billion valuation
items.summary: LangChain raised a USD 300 million Series C led by CapitalG, with GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP and Sapphire Ventures, at a USD 3 billion valuation, more than double its value a year ago, the company announced on 13 November, according to TechCrunch. It now sells LangSmith for building and managing agents and claims 7,000 customers.
items.why: Investors are backing model-neutral agent tooling while the labs bundle their own, which keeps an independent option open for banks wary of lock-in.

items.headline: Gartner sees AI lifting 2027 IT spending 18.3 percent to USD 5.96 trillion
items.summary: Worldwide IT spending excluding telecom services will reach USD 5.961 trillion in 2027, up 18.3 percent on 2026, Gartner forecast, according to Netzwoche. Data centre systems lead with 55.5 percent growth to USD 1,366 billion. Data centre demand has more than doubled memory prices in a year, a rise Gartner expects to last through 2027.
items.why: Dearer servers and memory will feed into bank IT budgets and private cloud plans just as boards set spending for next year.

items.headline: Galaxus opens its product catalogue to Claude and ChatGPT through MCP
items.summary: Digitec Galaxus launched a Model Context Protocol interface that lets AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT search its Swiss catalogue and show prices, ratings and review summaries in the chat, ICTjournal reported. It says it is the first Swiss retailer to offer one officially. Baskets and payment stay in its own shop for now.
items.why: A major Swiss retailer building for agent-led shopping brings the question JPMorgan faces at the card closer to Swiss issuers.

say_it_today: JPMorgan is fencing AI agents off at the card while Galaxus invites them into its catalogue: agent-led shopping is arriving from the retail side, and banks now decide whether it runs on bounded, tokenised credentials or on workarounds that cost merchants more.
